clean_consumer.notes: The checked-in corpus is dependency-free and bounded to the declared architecture cases.

real_consumer.notes: Immutable real consumer selection. Runtime is unavailable in this benchmark environment; no timing is invented.

setup_steps: Build or install cargo-octet at the pinned source revision.
Export standards/benchmark/corpus/octet-architecture.ncl and pass the checked policy.
Select the corpus scope explicitly; do not inherit an ambient workspace.
Install cargo-pup 0.1.9 from crates.io.
Declare the dependency-boundary and reexport rules in the reviewed tool configuration.
Run against the selected corpus targets and retain diagnostics verbatim.
Add archunit 0.0.2 as a test dependency in the consumer fixture.
Write the layer and dependency rules as a test module.
Run cargo test for that module and retain the test output.
Install the pinned Rust toolchain with the clippy component.
Select lints explicitly; the benchmark does not claim an architecture check.
Install cargo-deny 0.20.2.
Supply the reviewed deny.toml policy.
Run the dependency checks; this tool does not claim architecture or evidence assurance.
Install cargo-vet 0.10.3.
Configure the audit set and retain the fetched audit state.
Run cargo vet; this tool does not claim architecture or evidence assurance.
Install Semgrep 1.184.0.
Load the reviewed token-pattern rules and select the corpus path.
Retain SARIF or JSON output verbatim; macro and cfg outcomes remain partial.
Install the CodeQL CLI 2.27.4 and the Rust query pack.
Create the database from the corpus with the pinned compiler.
Run the reviewed queries and retain SARIF output verbatim.
Check out the pinned repository script.
Provide jq and sh, then run the script against each assurance fixture.
Retain the exit status; an unrun script is not clean evidence.

corpus.rationale: The application shell calls only the core-owned Port trait and constructs no adapter type.
The application shell reaches core internals and constructs an outbound adapter, violating the dependency rule.
Aliasing a core-owned port is a permitted public reexport.
The facade reexports outbound-adapter internals and constructs the adapter directly.
The macro expands only to the core-owned port method.
The macro hides an outbound-adapter construction from token-only callers but not from expansion-aware analysis.
The strict branch calls the port; the non-strict branch is inert and constructs nothing.
With default features the non-strict branch constructs the adapter; the analyzer must state the selected configuration.
Both feature branches contain the same direct adapter call; reviewers dispute whether this is one violation or two configuration-specific violations.
The call is expressed through the trait method on a dyn Trait receiver.
The call resolves to an inherent method on the concrete outbound adapter.
The composition-root binary wires an explicit port and constructs no adapter.
A separate workspace binary target constructs the outbound adapter outside the composition-root port path.
The selected child scope contains no Rust files; zero findings are not clean evidence of correctness.
The retained evidence identity differs from the identity the claim requires.
All retained identities agree, so a conforming assurance check accepts the claim.
The recorded policy identity differs from the currently checked policy identity.
The execution status is not_run, so no observed run supports the claim.
The proof source identity does not match the identity the linkage claims.

coverage_boundary.statement: The corpus is a small compiling fixture with declared compliant, violating, disputed, and empty-scope cases; it is not a complete Rust program or a representative sample of Rust projects.

negative_controls.description: A violating case that did not compile must not become a detection.
An observation whose case or source identity no longer matches the frozen oracle must be rejected.
An observation with a different analyzed scope must not enter comparable metrics.
Removing a timed-out observation must surface missing execution instead of clean evidence.
A derived comparison that does not reproduce from retained inputs must be rejected.
A differing toolchain or cache identity must be surfaced, not merged.
Unsupported scope must not increment clean evidence or true negatives.
The artifact must reject a complete-Rust-coverage claim for the bounded corpus.

non_claims: The experiment is bounded fixture evidence; it does not prove correctness, universal detection, complete Rust coverage, or release eligibility.
The experiment does not prove correctness, universal detection, or release eligibility.
Fixture observations are recorded evidence, not a claim that every candidate executable ran in this environment.
Unavailable tools remain unsupported; their absence is not clean evidence.
The bounded corpus is not complete Rust coverage and precision/recall apply only to declared comparable subsets.

dependency_differences: cargo-pup and ArchUnitRust require their own pinned crates; Octet runs from the pinned workspace build.
Semgrep and CodeQL are unavailable in this environment, so their runtime rows stay unavailable.
cargo-vet is unavailable and cargo-deny is unusable in the current shell; neither is counted as clean.

tasks.description: Application-shell code may not reach core internals or construct outbound adapters.
tasks.required_scope: selected source file and its declared crate role

tasks.description: Public reexports and aliases may expose core ports but not adapter internals.
tasks.required_scope: selected source file and its public item graph

tasks.description: Macro expansion may not hide a forbidden dependency or construction.
tasks.required_scope: selected source file and expansion-aware call graph

tasks.description: Cfg-selected branches must be attributed to the analyzed feature configuration.
tasks.required_scope: selected source file plus the declared feature and target configuration

tasks.description: Trait and inherent method references are resolved to the defining type or trait.
tasks.required_scope: selected source file and resolved method definitions

tasks.description: Every selected workspace target is analyzed with the same dependency rule.
An empty selection is neither clean evidence nor a false negative.
Retained evidence identities must still match the claim and the checked policy.
tasks.required_scope: retained evidence file and checked policy identity

tasks.description: Evidence admitted under a different policy identity is rejected.
A claim without an observed execution is rejected.
Proof artifacts must link to the source bytes the claim names.
tasks.required_scope: proof source identity and claimed source identity
